subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw land the bounded provider-normalized schema-parameter cache in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78664 now, or fold this issue into the broader prepared-runtime migration?
rationale: The repeated-normalization path is source-visible, but the permanent cache lifecycle and owner boundary affect provider hooks, custom provider behavior, plugin metadata preservation, and the prepared-runtime rollout.

options.title: Refresh and land the bounded cache
options.body: Land the internal parameter-only cache after provider/runtime review, keeping custom provider hooks uncached and avoiding a new public config surface.

options.title: Fold into prepared runtime
options.body: Keep this issue open until prepared runtime carries enough provider/tool facts to remove repeated hot-path work without a separate cache layer.

options.title: Require live proof first
options.body: Hold implementation until maintainers get current-main Google/Gemini or heap-profile before/after evidence from a real provider path.

recommendation.title: Refresh and land the bounded cache
recommendation.body: Land the internal parameter-only cache after provider/runtime review, keeping custom provider hooks uncached and avoiding a new public config surface.

likelyOwner.reason: mcaxtr owns the adjacent prepared-runtime tracker, which is the clearest decision point for whether this cache lands independently or waits for the broader migration.
